about: Evidence captures for three Friday pictures in plan-v6.json that had none: fri-claude-launch-pages, fri-deep-altman-same-day and fri-deep-openai-free-dec-2025. Real pages only, never redrawn, nothing added to the frame.
how: Playwright (Python) driving Chromium 1194 (/opt/pw-browsers): plain 1440x900 viewport screenshots at device scale 2, so every PNG is 2880x1800. Logged out, locale en-US, browser time zone UTC. Nothing was drawn on or injected into any page; the only interaction was clicking The Decoder's cookie-consent button ('Agree', its only one-click choice). Crop and mark boxes were measured from the live page (element boxes and exact text ranges); the Opus 5.5 hero is drawn on a WebGL canvas, so its boxes were measured from the capture's own pixels.
coordinates: Every crop, mark and other box is [x, y, w, h] in the capture's own pixels (2880x1800, origin top-left). 'mark' is one box around the words he talks about; 'mark_lines' gives the same words line by line where they wrap or stop mid-line, so a highlight does not spill onto the next words. 'also_mark' boxes are optional extras (a title, a time line).
rules_kept: No header strip, label or highlight is burned into any PNG; marks and the 'captured <date>' line are for the edit to draw.
Headlines are kept whole in their crops (The Decoder's carries '$300 billion valuation'; it is not ringed).
Altman's post is cropped whole, both sentences, with only the last sentence marked; its time line reads in UTC (6:11 PM, Mar 31, 2025).
The OpenAI funding sentence has a crop that stops right after '$40 billion' so the valuation he does not say stays out; crop_whole_sentence keeps it all.

unreachable.why: Paywall. The piece is in WIRED's 'Model Behavior' subscriber newsletter. A logged-out reader sees the header and one sentence, then 'Model Behavior is exclusive to subscribers.' Neither quoted line is rendered on the page (the text sits only in the page's hidden data, and revealing it would mean editing the page, which this task forbids).

alternatives.what: The WIRED reporter's own public post, 16 Dec 2025, 5:41 PM UTC, with WIRED's article card in it: 'The router—which was costly for the company to serve, but aimed to improve answer quality—was thought to be hurting engagement, one person familiar with the matter told WIRED.' Its words are 'costly for the company to serve', not WIRED's exact 'In practice' sentence, and it does not say 'seemed to send many more free users' to reasoning.

alternatives.for: steps 2 and 3, the exact WIRED lines
alternatives.what: Best real source: a capture of the same WIRED page from a subscriber's signed-in browser (Krish's, if he has WIRED), of the paragraphs 'In practice, the router seemed to send many more free users to OpenAI’s advanced reasoning models, which are more expensive for OpenAI to serve.' and 'An OpenAI spokesperson tells WIRED that the company determined, based on user feedback, that Free and Go users preferred staying in the default chat experience'. The only open pages carrying these lines are a news-scraper copy (https://ng.headtopics.com/news/openai-rolls-back-chatgpt-s-model-router-system-for-most-77262276) and a Mastodon post quoting it (https://tldr.nettime.org/@remixtures/115736616072887427); neither is fit to show on screen as WIRED.

unreachable.related_fact: OpenAI's own release note (capture -1, the paragraph continuing past the frame's bottom edge) gives its reason as 'To maximize choice, free users will now use GPT-5.2 Instant by default'. It does not say users preferred the default; that reason exists only in WIRED's spokesperson quote.
